entry = await rlm.harness.create_memory(title="ARC paired boundary bars project marker rays", content="For ARC grids with two parallel equal-length boundary bars of one color and one or more isolated marker pixels of a second color, each marker selects an offset along the bar nearest/containing its aligned coordinate. Project a ray of the marker color inward from that bar at the marker's position until the marker; replace the marker cell with color 4 and stop. Transfer the same offset to the opposite parallel bar and project an inward ray from it in the opposite direction; if unobstructed it continues to the grid edge. Preserve both bars and other cells. Offsets are measured from the bar's start along its length (as with horizontal bars, marker offset 1 on bottom bar maps to offset 1 on top bar). Example 10x8: horizontal 7 bars at row0 cols0-2 and row9 cols4-6, marker 8 at (6,5): draw 8 down from top-bar offset1 at col1 through row9, draw 8 upward from bottom at col5 rows7-8, change marker (6,5) to4. This also generalizes to vertical bars: the equal-offset rays are horizontal. Test solved: bg6, vertical 1 bars at c11 rows0-1 and c0 rows2-3, marker7 at (r2,c2): row0 c0..10 becomes7, row2 c1=7, marker c2 becomes4; retain the bars.", path="arc", global_=True)
print(entry)
